extraction.Name: Margaret Provost, nee Cottier
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee to her 160 acre allotment when she got it, but the Indian Agency advised her that she would either have to take it or lose it thru taxes; so she accepted it under protest
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold her allotment in 1924 to pay the taxes
extraction.Buyer: I. R. Trueblood, who paid the taxes and gave her $700.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Bennett County gave her thirty days time in which to sell her allotment to pay the taxes, so she sold it; the taxes forced her to sell
extraction.Occupation/Income: husband farms his allotment for a living, which, being his only income, makes a slim one
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has poor health, being troubled with her heart; has a husband who has good health and who supports her and her one child, who is in possession of good health; she considers $700.00 was a poor price for her land; has never received any help from the County, State or United States Government; document sworn November 23, 1928; allotment was 160 acres | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County / Pine Ridge area (not explicitly stated)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
